implementation_notes: .NET 6+ ships PriorityQueue<TElement,TPriority>, which supplies the ordered pending window without a third-party library; SortedDictionary<long, Msg> is the alternative when arbitrary removal (duplicates, reject old, capacity eviction) is required. System.Threading.Channels provides the order-preserving handoff and a natural cancellation point, and a CancellationTokenSource with CancelAfter implements the gap deadline. The cursor, capacity and duplicates policy stay application code, so the structure is hand-written; when the disorder originates below the process boundary, broker-side ordering (Azure Service Bus sessions, or a saga that models the sequence explicitly) is the better first answer.
pitfalls: PriorityQueue<TElement,TPriority> is not thread safe and offers no arbitrary Remove, so a resequencer that must evict or reject by sequence number needs SortedDictionary or its own index.
await foreach over a Channel completes while the window may still hold messages ahead of a gap; drain explicitly on completion instead of dropping the buffer.
CancellationTokenSource is single-use: re-create or reset it per gap window, otherwise the timeout stays permanently signalled and the policy fires on every message.
